objects.name: Christopher Columbus
objects.description: Italian explorer who completed four voyages across the Atlantic Ocean, opening the way for widespread European exploration and colonization of the Americas

objects.name: Hernán Cortés
objects.description: Spanish Conquistador who led an expedition that caused the fall of the Aztec Empire and brought large portions of what is now mainland Mexico under the rule of the King of Castile

objects.name: Francisco Pizarro
objects.description: Spanish conquistador who conquered the Incan Empire

entries.locationName: Departure from Palos de la Frontera
entries.description: Columbus departed from the port of Palos de la Frontera, Spain, with three ships: the Niña, the Pinta, and the Santa María. This marked the beginning of his first voyage to the New World.
sources: Historia de las Indias by Bartolomé de las Casas

entries.description: The fleet stopped at the Canary Islands for repairs and supplies. The Pinta's rudder needed fixing, and they restocked provisions before continuing west into the unknown Atlantic.

entries.locationName: First Landing in the New World
entries.description: Columbus landed on an island in the Bahamas, which he named San Salvador. The indigenous people called it Guanahani. This moment marked the first European contact with the Americas, changing world history forever.
sources: The Diario of Christopher Columbus's First Voyage to America

entries.description: Columbus arrived at the coast of Cuba, believing it to be part of mainland Asia. He explored the northern coast of Cuba for several weeks.
Pizarro captured the Incan emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca
sources: Chronicle of Peru by Pedro Cieza de León
